claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes pesting or unacceptable oxygen degradation during high-temperature air exposure.
3D ink extrusion printing followed by hydrogen de-binding and titanium-sponge-gettered vacuum sintering will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr relative to the as-cast state.
The proposed processing route will refine the alloy microstructure.
The proposed processing route will reduce porosity.
Controlling the sintering environment and using a titanium-sponge getter will lower oxygen incorporation into the alloy.
Titanium sponge acts as an oxygen getter during vacuum sintering and reduces residual oxygen in the processing atmosphere.
Reduced processing-stage oxygen uptake will promote formation of a uniform, adherent, and stable oxide scale during subsequent exposure.
A uniform, adherent oxide scale will resist further oxidation and pesting.
The controlled printing and sintering steps will refine the microstructure without degrading mechanical properties.
The processed alloy will exhibit significantly reduced pesting relative to cast material during a 5-hour exposure to ambient air at approximately 800 °C.
After processing, the alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility in the range of 8–16%.
After processing, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
